quote: Yeah. Yeah. And, actually, you guys are, like, the folks that my neighbor used used.
stewart_read: This is an unsolicited social-proof signal — the customer volunteers that a neighbor already used Ion. The rep acknowledges it ('Oh, actually? Okay. Cool.') and asks the neighbor's name for lookup purposes, but never uses the referral to build curiosity or trust ('that's great, we love when neighbors are on the same street — did you see what their system looked like?').
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to treat neighbor-referral mentions as a trust-building anchor, not just a database lookup — a quick reflective question keeps the warmth alive instead of moving straight into name-verification logistics.

stewart_read: This is a reasonable operational follow-up to locate the referral record, but it's purely administrative — the rep pivots immediately to data lookup rather than acknowledging why the referral matters to the customer's confidence in Ion.
alternative_hypothesis: The reactive read (rep missed a rapport opportunity) is more supported than a strategic read here — there's no evidence the rep intended to circle back to the referral value later in the call.
coaching_implication: Small moment, but worth flagging alongside the enthusiasm-signal note above as a joint teaching point: verify the name, but also mirror value back to the customer.

stewart_read: The 02:36-03:47 stretch is garbled cross-talk while the customer navigates the Dominion website live on the call — names get confused (Carter, McConnell) and there's a long silent gap before the rep resumes at 03:47. This reads as an unscripted tech-navigation wait rather than a rep error, but the dead air is notable.
alternative_hypothesis: Could reflect a diarization/transcription artifact given the confused names, rather than an actual customer misunderstanding of rep identity.
coaching_implication: Not a coaching fault on the rep's part, but worth noting for QA — a nearly 50-second live gap while the customer logs into the utility site is exactly the kind of dead air Ion's elerly/low-tech alternative-path protocol addresses (bill_collection.alternative_paths); here it resolved fine, but the rep didn't proactively offer a verbal read-back shortcut before letting the wait run.

quote: And you guys have to, like, basically, you have to do it in site inspection?
stewart_read: Customer is checking process expectations before committing to a specific time — a legitimate logistics question, not a stall or objection. The rep resolves it in two lines and offers the phone-call format the customer prefers.
coaching_implication: Rep handled this cleanly and immediately offered the lower-friction option (phone call vs. in-person) — worth noting as a positive example of quick, confident logistics handling.

stewart_read: The customer reads off both a dollar range ($5.24-$6.99) and an average kWh figure (846) live from the utility site. The rep captures the numbers mechanically ('Cool. And then it was last month, it was $5.24. Is that just the lowest?') but never reflects the numbers back as a hook — no 'that's a great baseline for us to build your savings estimate against' or similar forward-pulling line.
alternative_hypothesis: A strategic read might argue the rep intentionally deferred deeper bill discussion to the closer's design-review call — but there's no verbal signal ('we'll dig into that on the call with the specialist') supporting that as a deliberate choice rather than an omission.
coaching_implication: This is the clearest missed anchor on the call. Coach the rep to use one line acknowledging the number before moving to scheduling — reinforces the reason the appointment matters.

quote: As far as scheduling goes, is it better to meet with you in the mornings or afternoons?
stewart_read: The rep moves cleanly through scheduling and eventually locks a day and time (Tuesday 6PM), but the call closes without the full button-up sequence — no explicit 'is that fair?' handshake, no no-driving/computer instruction, though a text-confirmation promise is made.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive gap, not strategic: nothing in the call suggests the rep intentionally skipped the handshake for a later purpose — the call simply ends after the time is set and a text promise is given.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to always close with the explicit fairness check and the no-driving/computer instruction — both are tied to show-rate per Ion's button-up protocol, and both were skipped here despite an otherwise smooth booking.
